previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for her sixth cycle of high-dose methotrexate for primary colonic diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with CNS involvement. The chemotherapy was administered at a reduced dose of 3500 mg/m² and was well tolerated without mucositis. Leucovorin rescue was initiated 24 hours post-infusion, and methotrexate levels declined appropriately, becoming undetectable by the third day. She received IVIG for common variable immune deficiency and pentamidine for PJP prophylaxis, though she experienced transient shortness of breath after pentamidine that resolved with albuterol. A concurrent C. difficile infection was diagnosed and treated with oral vancomycin. Her diabetes was managed by holding metformin during admission, and she was discharged home with medication adjustments and close follow-up. She remained stable throughout the stay and was discharged in good condition.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ woman with CVID and DLBCL lymphoma to colon and CNS 
admitted for cycle #7 high-dose methotrexate.  Considering 
recent high-ostomy output and hypomagnesemia, she was initially 
hydrated and repleted with magnesium sulfate before starting 
chemo.  The following day, her neutropenia was worse, so chemo 
was held an additional day.  The neutropenia stabilized, so 
high-dose MTX was administered.  She tolerated this without 
difficulty and was discharged once the MTX level was <0.05.
.
# DLBCL: s/p high-dose MTX 3.5g/m2 ___ followed by 
leucovorin rescue 24hrs later.  Bicarb was administered 
throughout to enhance MTX excretion.  She was discharged home 
once the MTX was <0.05.

IgM negative, IgG positive.  CMV PCR negative.  Parvovirus IgM 
negative, IgG positive.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted for cycle #7 high-dose methotrexate for 
diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of your brain.  This was initially 
held to provide you with IV fluids for hydration considering 
your recent high-ostomy output and possible dehydration.  A low 
magnesium level was also repleted with IV magnesium.  
Chemotherapy was held an additional day because of a low white 
blood cell count.  The low count remained stable, so chemo was 
given and you tolerated this well.  NO NEW MEDICATIONS except, 
you will continue to take Leucovorin by mouth for 3 doses after 
discharge.
